summary: Of the 25 filed reviews, 24 accurately describe their node's own samples, ground their verdicts in real (verified) defects or genuine strengths, and are not transplantable templates -- each rationale quotes stems specific to that node and several reviews surface non-obvious, verified cross-node content bleed (e.g. mg_q1_0's seeds 605/606 duplicating sibling nodes' items verbatim, na_q1_1's seeds 600/601 being byte-identical to na_q1_2, na_q1_7's seed 613 belonging to na_q1_8's commutative-property scope). One node, mat_g1_na_q1_8, is voided: its comprehensive_coverage finding falsely claims no sampled item uses zero as an addend, when seed 45 ('0 + 2 = ___') plainly does -- a factual error about the node's own sample data rather than a defensible judgment call, even though the node's overall FAIL verdict remains independently defensible on its other (accurate) findings. A second node, mat_g1_mg_q2_2, contains an unverifiable and likely false aside about a sibling node's sample content (claims mg_q2_0 shares its broken 'non_standard' placeholder text, which is absent from mg_q2_0's packet) but this does not affect its own-node findings or verdict, so it was flagged rather than voided. Independent re-judgment on 5 pseudo-randomly selected nodes (mat_g1_dp_q3_0, mat_g1_mg_q1_2, mat_g1_mg_q2_0, mat_g1_na_q1_1, mat_g1_na_q1_8) produced identical verdicts to the filed reviews in all 5 cases, a 0% disagreement rate. With only one voided node and zero disagreement in the independent sample, batch B1 is reliable overall, with the two flagged accuracy issues (one hallucinated absence, one unverifiable cross-node claim) worth correcting but not indicative of systemic template-reuse or unearned verdicts.
